(1) InputStreamHelper.java: after `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName())`, it computes `dir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator` and throws IOException if `file.getCanonicalPath()` does not start with it. The guard is correctly placed before both the directory branch (mkdirsQuietly) and the FileOutputStream write path, covering all three alert traces (lines 129, 136/parent, 139/file). Appending File.separator correctly prevents sibling-prefix false negatives (e.g. dir vs dir-evil). Legitimate nested entries (nested/data.txt) still resolve inside dir and extract normally. IOException is already the declared/handled exception type for this method, so no new failure surface for callers. (2) Adds a new JUnit test InputStreamHelperTest.java exercising both rejection and valid-entry paths — test-only, does not weaken the fix. pov.diff only adds POV harness files and does not modify project source; the patcher did not alter or disable the POV. No unrelated or broad behavior changes.
